question: Which of the following liquids can dissolve noble metals such as gold and platinum?
solution:
The correct answer is__** **____**Aqua regia**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Aqua regia, also known as **king's water**, is a** mixture of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid** in the ratio 1:3 and is used to dissolve noble metals such as gold and platinum.
 
• Only the combination of two acids is capable to dissolve various elements, while individually both HCl and HNO3 are not capable to dissolve them.
 
• It is a **yellow-orange fuming liquid** used to remove metals like gold and platinum from substances, especially in **microelectronics and micro-fabrication labs**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Formic Acid:**

 
• The simplest form of carboxylic acid, formic acid is present in the venom of red ants. 
 
• Due to its stinging nature, it is used by the ants to kill prey or to protect their nests from predators.
 
• In the case of humans, it is mainly used as a preservative due to its anti-bacterial nature. It is also used in the production of leather, rubber, and cleaning products.

**Acetic Acid:**

 
• Acetic acid is the common name of **ethanoic acid.**
 
• The chemical Formulae for Acetic acid is **CH3COOH.**
 
• It belongs to a group called carboxylic acid and hence they are **weak acids**.
 
• When acetic acid is diluted in water with a percentage of 5-8, then **vinegar** is formed.
 
• The melting point of acetic acid is 290K and it often freezes at room temperature, hence it has another name called **Glacial Acetic Acid.**

**Chloroform:**

 
• Chloroform, or trichloromethane, is an organic compound with the formula **CHCl₃**.
 
• It is a **colorless, volatile, liquid** derivative of trichloromethane with an ether-like odor.
 
• Formerly used as an inhaled** anaesthetic** during the surgery, the primary use of chloroform today is as a **solvent** and in the production of the** refrigerant freon.**
